title: NetWasm 0.10 Speeds Up C# on WebAssembly, Now Faster Than Mono AOT
gist: NetWasm, an ahead-of-time C#-to-WebAssembly compiler and runtime, reports that its 0.10.x optimisation series (exception handling, bounds-check elimination, Wasm SIMD, division) makes it 0.41x Mono AOT's time on a 2,213-case geometric mean, with self-reported Wasmtime/M1 Max benchmarks also showing remaining gaps versus desktop .NET on vector and math workloads.

themes.theme: Benchmark standing vs Mono AOT and desktop .NET

insights.claim: Across 2,213 benchmark cases, NetWasm 0.10.8 at O3 with NetWasmGC takes 0.41 times Mono AOT's time as a geometric mean (excluding five cases where Mono's LLVM removes the work), with family ratios from 0.34 for intrinsics to 0.81 for math.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: A third-party compiler outperforming Microsoft's own Mono AOT on WebAssembly signals C# could become more viable for Wasm/WASI targets.

insights.claim: NetWasm's geometric-mean ratio against desktop .NET 11 RC3 JIT fell to 0.87 in 0.10.8 from 2.15 in 0.10.6.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Rapid closing of the gap to native .NET makes WebAssembly a more credible deployment target for C# workloads.
insights.locator: Against desktop .NET 11 RC3 JIT the ratio is 0.87

insights.claim: A 120-frame DoomSharp render takes 1,623 ms on NetWasmGC versus 2,371 ms on Mono AOT and 1,053 ms on desktop .NET JIT.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Real-application workloads confirm NetWasm leads Mono AOT but still trails native JIT.

insights.claim: NetWasm's benchmarks are self-reported from a single machine (Apple M1 Max) and single runtime (Wasmtime 49.0.3), and identical loops at different addresses varied by up to 15%, so results elsewhere may differ.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Treat the performance claims as preliminary until independently reproduced.

insights.claim: Wasmtime adds register save-and-restore code around any function that can throw or catch, so routing throws through a shared function in NetWasm 0.10.1 cut a UI churn benchmark from 17.6 to 7.9 ms.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Exception-handling overhead is a key performance tax for managed languages on Wasm runtimes.
insights.locator: Much of the early gain came from exception handling

insights.claim: NetWasm 0.10.7 lowers Vector128, Vector<T> and PackedSimd to 128-bit Wasm SIMD; with hoisted Math calls a Burgers' equation solver dropped from 497 ms to 71 ms, versus 186 ms for Mono AOT and 93 ms for desktop .NET.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Wasm SIMD can let numeric C# code match or beat native in specific cases, broadening scientific/compute use cases for Wasm.

insights.claim: Inlining and bounds-check elimination in NetWasm 0.10.2 cut a 100,000-integer quicksort from 77.2 ms to 54.0 ms, overtaking Mono AOT's 58.0 ms, while 0.10.8 division optimisations cut a trial-division test from 1,376 to 765 ms versus 862 ms for Mono AOT.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Shows classic compiler optimisations still yield large gains on young Wasm toolchains.

insights.claim: Desktop .NET remains about 3.1 times faster than NetWasm on vector benchmarks because it uses host SIMD directly while WebAssembly is limited to fixed 128-bit operations.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Wasm's fixed-width SIMD caps performance for vector-heavy workloads; watch for wider SIMD proposals.
insights.locator: The article is open about what is left.

insights.claim: NetWasm's NewtR workload regressed to 1.9 times slower than in 0.10.6, which the authors attribute to Wasmtime's register allocator keeping a value in a stack slot around the loop; Math.Pow is 1.4x and CopyBlock64 3.3x slower than Mono AOT.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Wasm runtime code-generation quality is a bottleneck outside the compiler author's control.
insights.locator: The article is open about what is left.
